n: Foreign Terrorist Fighter Travel and Support Financing
ds: Individuals who travel to join terrorist groups abroad, and networks that support them, finance their journeys through personal funds, loans, family transfers and cash. Financial signals typically cluster around the preparatory period before travel and continue through remittances to the destination region.

src.t: FATF, Financing of the Terrorist Organisation Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) (2015)
UN Security Council Resolution 2178 (2014) on foreign terrorist fighters

cn.rt: Pre-travel account run-down, cash withdrawals, card use on transit routes and borrowing before departure.

rat: Pre-travel account emptying, borrowing and ATM use abroad.

ind.n: Closure of accounts and withdrawal of savings before travel
ind.cx: Customer empties accounts, cancels commitments or sells possessions in a short interval without clear purpose.
ind.fp: Emigration, study abroad and relocation are common legitimate reasons.
ind.ds: Customer empties accounts, cancels commitments or sells possessions in a short interval without clear purpose.

ind.n: Card and ATM use at transit points near conflict zones
ind.cx: Card or ATM activity in locations commonly used as transit routes to conflict areas, followed by cessation of usage.
ind.fp: Tourism, trade, humanitarian and diaspora travel produce overlapping footprints.
ind.ds: Cash withdrawals, ATM or card use occur at transit points or border regions near conflict zones.
ind.cn: Cash or card use in border and transit areas near conflict zones

ind.n: Remittances from family or associates to individuals in border areas
ind.cx: Recurrent small transfers to recipients in or near conflict zones with no clear family relationship or humanitarian need.
ind.fp: Diaspora families routinely support relatives in affected regions.
ind.ds: Recurrent small transfers to recipients in or near conflict zones with no clear family relationship or humanitarian need.

ind.n: Loans or credit taken with no repayment intent
ind.cx: Customer obtains borrowing and then leaves the jurisdiction, defaulting.
ind.fp: Job loss and financial trouble cause defaults.
ind.ds: Customer obtains borrowing and then leaves the jurisdiction, defaulting.

ind.n: Purchase of equipment commonly carried by fighters
ind.cx: Retail purchases of outdoor, protective, communication or medical gear in unusual quantity shortly before travel.
ind.fp: Hiking, camping and humanitarian volunteering generate the same purchases.
ind.ds: Retail purchases of outdoor, protective, communication or medical gear in unusual quantity shortly before travel.

ind.n: Connections to known facilitators or recruiters
ind.cx: Customer transacts with parties identified in public or law enforcement material as facilitators of travel.
ind.fp: Social contacts and shared community groups cause innocent links.
ind.ds: Customer transacts, including in small amounts, with persons identified in public or law-enforcement material as facilitators or subjects of prior reports.
ind.cn: Dealings with known facilitators or persons on investigative watch lists

ind.n: Travel booked to destination near conflict via indirect route
ind.cx: Itineraries with unusual routing, one-way tickets and short-notice booking inconsistent with customer profile.
ind.fp: Budget travellers, migrants and workers regularly use multi-leg routes.
ind.ds: Itineraries with unusual routing, one-way tickets and short-notice booking inconsistent with customer profile.

ind.n: Minors or young adults funded by third parties
ind.cx: Accounts of young customers receive small repeated funds from unrelated adults, followed by cash-out.
ind.fp: Gifting from relatives and part-time work are normal.
ind.ds: Accounts of young customers receive small repeated funds from unrelated adults, followed by cash-out.

ctl.ds: Contacts the customer, or the relationship manager does so, to obtain and record an explanation of unusual transactions, relationships or recipients, and to test it against evidence. The answer informs whether activity is legitimate or should be escalated.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.
Tracks changes to regulation, disclosure regimes and national threat assessments and updates rules, location lists and procedures accordingly. It keeps controls aligned with the current threat.

Independently verifies stated income, employment, obligations and application facts against third-party, bureau and prior-history data at origination. It reduces application, credit and insurance fraud.
Verifies lender ownership, loan terms and rationale, collateral origin and repayment sources, and alerts on early or third-party repayment. It prevents loans being used to place or layer funds.

Teaches analysts to weigh several weak signals together, understand network and settlement structures, and avoid profiling on protected characteristics. It raises investigative quality and reduces both missed risk and unfair outcomes.

Translates published and sanitised typologies and red flags into targeted monitoring scenarios and context-aware rules that are reviewed periodically. It aligns monitoring with known criminal methods.
Checks parties against previously filed internal reports, links to reported accounts and feeds report outcomes back into tuning. It spots repeat subjects and sharpens detection.

ctl.n: Suspicion escalation and reporting decision protocol
ctl.ds: Defines timelines, owners and criteria for escalating concerns and deciding whether to report, and for documents implying payments to proscribed groups. It ensures timely, accountable decisions.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.

Provides discreet escalation routes and private conversation procedures so staff can refer suspected victims of exploitation, coercion or trafficking to specialists, police and support organisations. It prioritises victim safety.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.
